raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t chase fancy things. On my 12 mu, I still do wheat and maize the same as most people here, because this way the land doesn’t sit empty and even if one crop is weaker, the other still brings something back. We only have two people at home, so I need a plan we can manage ourselves, with maybe a little hired machine work at the busy time. For wheat, I will sow in early October after the summer maize is off, use the seed people around here usually buy, and put fertilizer under it once at sowing, then add a bit more when it starts standing up strong in spring if the leaves look pale. Water costs money from the well, but wheat in our place cannot rely on sky water alone, so I’ll probably water about three times, not too many, not too few. For maize, after wheat harvest I have to move fast, no dawdling, because the season is tight. I’ll use hybrid seed, do simple rotary tillage or direct sow right after harvest, put some fertilizer at planting, and if the maize looks weak later I’ll add a little more. If rain is decent, I won’t irrigate much; if it turns dry at tasseling, I’ll give water then because that affects yield badly. I don’t count very fine like educated people do. I mostly follow what worked on my own land and what the good households nearby do, while keeping enough cash in hand so the two of us are not left with nothing if something goes wrong.
